A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same symmetry-discovery framework. All 25 pages of v2 and 20 pages of v4, including appendices, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original regression, physical-system, and top-quark-tagging results, together with appendix noise experiments and learned-generator analyses.

after.justification: v4 reports original predictive and symmetry-recovery results in Tables 2–3 and 5–6, plus parabolic learning dynamics and sample-size/noise experiments in Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: The joint optimization of the orientation, rates, and predictor through canonicalization is retained; all three geometric representations already appear in v2 Sections 8–10. v4 revises the hyperbolic layer to handle both sectors through an additional canonicalization branch (Definition 3.2) and introduces a learnable center for non-origin rotations (Appendix C.1). These are component-level procedural changes.

E1.justification: v4 adds phase-coupled Angled Sine regression and regression on dense 4×4 matrices with a hidden rank-one shear symmetry. Its polynomial u(x) retains the earlier q/r construction family and differs from v2's norm-valued u(x). The separate p(x), norm-valued u(x), and anisotropic-quantum evaluations disappear, although quantum models remain mentioned in the introduction. Pendulum, inertia, and jet-tagging coverage is retained.

E2.justification: EMLP is removed from the evaluated comparisons. LieGAN and LieGG disappear from their earlier polynomial and physical-task comparisons but remain evaluated on Angled Sine in Appendix G.3. Augerino becomes the primary comparator and gains an explicit top-tagging comparison in Table 3; v2 instead reports comparison with an unnamed full-Lorentz approach.

E3.justification: The reported training budget changes from 100 to 50 epochs, and the regression backbone changes from a four-layer network to five specified hidden layers. Generator evaluation changes from cosine distance against a reference generator to cosine similarity against a projection onto the reference Lie algebra. v4 also introduces elliptic-versus-hyperbolic jet evaluation and sample-size/noise sweeps. These changes prevent treating revised scores as same-setting comparisons.

E4.justification: v4 adds Angled Sine sample-efficiency comparisons across 8K–64K samples, noise sensitivity across dataset sizes, and parabolic generator-recovery dynamics (Figures 3–4). These replace v2's Gaussian-noise experiments on u(x)/r(x) and its learned-versus-reference basis analyses and heatmaps. The questions tested and supporting evidence change substantially.

E5.justification: Mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting is retained and extended to pendulum, inertia, and top-tagging results previously presented as individual estimates. However, v2's explicit three-independent-seed statement disappears; v4 does not specify the run counts underlying its uncertainties. This establishes a reporting change, not a demonstrated change in the number of runs.

E6.justification: Results are substantially replaced and expanded. For example, the proposed model's pendulum MSE changes from 5.59×10^-6 in v2 Table 5.2 to (2.0±0.1)×10^-4 in v4 Table 2. The earlier 88.03% jet accuracy is replaced by 83.0±0.1% for the elliptic variant and 84.4±0.4% for the hyperbolic variant. Angled Sine and parabolic results are added, while the explicit rotation-rate table is removed. Changed settings preclude interpreting these as direct performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Beyond the three-regime theory already present in v2, v4 introduces admissible domains, integer elliptic rates, explicit paired hyperbolic eigenvalues, and a nilpotency-index-two restriction. It revises the hyperbolic definition, supplies explicit noncompact proofs, and adds a Lipschitz bound and a general equivariance proposition. The earlier subgroup-equivalence Proposition B.1 is removed. The new Appendix F equivariance proof contains a sign inconsistency.

C1.justification: Although v2 includes generalized constructions later in the document, its abstract, contributions, and conclusion focus on SO(n). v4 makes joint discovery across elliptical, hyperbolic, and parabolic regimes the central contribution, emphasizing provable structural interpretability and empirical support for compact and noncompact symmetries. It also explicitly conditions discovery on a geometric regime supplied in advance.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive arguments about avoiding identity collapse, distinguishing one-parameter invariants from blockwise norms, and discouraging incorrect symmetries through increased Lipschitz complexity. Its limitations explicitly address assumed regimes and higher-order nilpotent generators. It also corrects the inertia task's symmetry description to simultaneous diagonal rotations, while replacing v2's detailed interpretation of learned/reference basis equivalence.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies 32K/64K sample counts, hidden widths, and matrix-shear data-generation equations. Conversely, it removes v2's Adam optimizer, 10^-3 learning rate, RTX A6000 hardware disclosure, and implementation-access link. These substantially change reproducibility information; the newly supplied sample counts do not establish increases over v2.

R1.justification: The central positioning against post-hoc discovery and augmentation-based invariance remains. v4 adds InfGen and BeyondAffine to the conceptual comparison, refines comparator classifications and the rationale for prioritizing Augerino, and adds references supporting noncompact geometry, jet physics, and phase coupling. Several earlier equivariance and SO(n)-focused references are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contributions, results narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The separate SO(n) and subsequent SL(n) treatments become one integrated method section; background moves to the appendix, and discussion, limitations, proofs, and experiments are reorganized. The model is renamed Hγ-Net, and the leftover acknowledgment-template instructions in v2 are removed.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column main text and substantially redesigns the architecture diagram and comparison tables. It adds a notation table and learning-dynamics/sensitivity plots, removes the orbit-correspondence illustration and basis heatmaps, and moves inertia results into the appendix. The exponential-map illustration is retained. These are extensive display and layout changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v4 integrates the previously disconnected generalized framework, corrects hyperbolic sector handling, states important scope restrictions, and adds direct noncompact experiments. However, comparison coverage and reproducibility disclosures shrink. Its new equivariance proof in Appendix F uses t0(x')=t0(x)-t but then factors the transformation with g(t), conflicting with Appendix D's positive shift. The empirical and explanatory gains coexist with unresolved support for central guarantees and reduced reproducibility, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
